documents.title: History and Physical - Admission
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of note: 03:40, HD1
Pt: 56-year-old male presenting via ED with fever, rigors, flank pain, and near-syncope.
HPI:
Onset of dysuria and urinary frequency approx 4 days prior to arrival, self-treated with fluids and OTC analgesic.
Over prior 24 h developed shaking chills, right flank ache, nausea with two episodes of emesis, progressive weakness.
Wife reports he became confused while walking to the bathroom tonight and was unable to stand without assistance.
No cough, no sputum, no pleuritic pain. No diarrhea. No abdominal surgery. No rash.
Arrived ED 02:10. Temperature 39.4 C at triage. Immediately flagged for sepsis pathway.
PMH:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, 8 years, last A1c reported by pt as 7.8 percent.
Hypertension. Nephrolithiasis with one prior stone passage. BPH with intermittent nocturia.
Former smoker, quit approx 10 years ago, 15 pack-years. Alcohol: 2-3 beers weekly. No illicit drugs.
Home medications:
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID
Lisinopril 20 mg PO daily
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO nightly
Atorvastatin 20 mg PO nightly
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family hx: father with CAD, mother with T2DM. No known renal disease.
ROS: positive for fever, chills, dysuria, flank pain, myalgias, lightheadedness. Negative for chest pain, dyspnea at rest, hematemesis, melena.
Vitals: T 38.9 C, HR 124, BP 84/48, RR 28, SpO2 95 percent on 2 L NC.
General: ill-appearing, diaphoretic, rigoring intermittently.
HEENT: dry mucous membranes, no scleral icterus.
Cardiac: tachycardic, regular, no murmur, no JVD.
Lungs: clear bilaterally, no crackles, tachypneic with shallow effort.
Abdomen: soft, right CVA tenderness marked, suprapubic tenderness mild, no rebound or guarding.
GU: no scrotal swelling, no perineal crepitus or tenderness.
Extremities: warm, cap refill 3 s, no edema.
Neuro: arouses to voice, oriented to person and place, not to situation; no focal deficit.
Skin: no petechiae, no purpura.
LABS AND STUDIES:
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30.
WBC 21,300 with 14% bands. Hgb 13.4, Hct 40.1.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Na 133, K 4.6, Cl 99, HCO3 18, BUN 38, glucose 244. Total bili 1.6, ALT 34, AST 41, INR 1.3.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
Portable CXR: no consolidation, no effusion.
Renal US at bedside: no hydronephrosis, no perinephric collection, mild right renal echogenicity change.
RESUSCITATION SO FAR:
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 mcg/kg/min to keep MAP above 65.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added.
ASSESSMENT:
Septic shock, presumed urinary source (acute pyelonephritis) in a diabetic male. Fluid-refractory hypotension now on vasopressor support.
Acute kidney injury, likely combined prehypertension/ischemic ATN physiology. Thrombocytopenia consistent with sepsis.
PLAN:
1. ICU admission, arterial line, central access. Hourly MAP goal above 65.
2. Continue broad-spectrum coverage; de-escalate per culture data.
3. Lactate clearance q2h until under 2.0. Strict I/O, Foley to gravity.
4. Hold lisinopril and metformin. SSI for glucose. Renal-dose all meds.
5. Urology consult if obstruction or abscess develops on repeat imaging.
6. VTE ppx with SCDs given platelets 84,000; reassess heparin ppx daily.
7. Updated wife at bedside 03:35, discussed shock physiology and ICU transfer.

documents.title: ICU Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 07:15
Subjective: Pt awake, more coherent, oriented x3 this morning. Reports flank pain improved from 8/10 to 4/10. Tolerated ice chips.
Overnight events: norepinephrine weaned from 0.12 to 0.04 mcg/kg/min by 06:00. One additional 500 mL NS for MAP 62 at 01:30. No arrhythmia.
Vitals 06:45: T 37.6 C, HR 96, BP 104/60, MAP 74, RR 20, SpO2 96 percent on 2 L NC.
Urine output 0.7 mL/kg/h over prior 8 h, up from 0.2 mL/kg/h at admission.
Exam:
General: alert, no rigors. Mucous membranes moist.
Cardiac: regular, no new murmur. Lungs clear, no crackles.
Abdomen: soft, mild right CVA tenderness, less than admission.
Extremities: warm, no edema, no digital ischemia on norepinephrine.
Labs 05:40: WBC 17,800, platelets 96,000, creatinine 2.1, HCO3 21, lactate 1.9.
Hx of admission labs reviewed: lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000 at presentation, now improving.
Micro: blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics, gram stain pending read.
Assessment: Septic shock secondary to urinary source, improving. Lactate cleared. AKI resolving with perfusion restoration. Thrombocytopenia recovering.
Plan:
1. Continue wean of norepinephrine, off when MAP sustained above 65 without support.
2. Continue piperacillin-tazobactam renally dosed and vancomycin; trough with next dose.
3. Repeat BMP and CBC this afternoon. Trend creatinine.
4. Continue Foley, strict I/O, maintenance fluids at 75 mL/h.
5. Hold lisinopril and metformin. SSI q4h, glucose 168 at 06:00.
6. Add heparin ppx once platelets above 100,000.
7. Anticipate step-down to floor later today if off pressors.

documents.title: ICU Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2, 16:30
Interval events: norepinephrine discontinued at 12:40 after 2 h at 0.02 mcg/kg/min. No hypotension since.
Vitals 16:00: T 37.2 C, HR 84, BP 118/68, MAP 84, RR 18, SpO2 97 percent on room air. Weaned off NC at 14:00.
Urine output 1.1 mL/kg/h since noon. Net positive 3.4 L since arrival.
Micro update: blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours. Urine culture with gram-negative rods, speciation pending; susceptibilities pending.
Antibiotic plan: vancomycin discontinued at 15:10 given gram-negative bacteremia and no MRSA risk features; continued on IV antibiotics with piperacillin-tazobactam.
Recap of initial dosing: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added.
Afternoon labs 14:20: WBC 13,400, platelets 112,000, creatinine 1.6, BUN 27, HCO3 23, lactate 1.3.
Exam:
Alert, oriented, sitting up in chair, ambulated to door with RN and one-person assist.
Cardiac regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, minimal right CVA tenderness.
No rash, no petechiae. Peripheral IV sites clean.
Assessment:
E. coli bacteremia with acute pyelonephritis and resolved septic shock. Off vasopressors, lactate normalized, AKI improving, platelets recovering.
Plan:
1. Transfer to medical floor this evening, telemetry not required.
2. Continue piperacillin-tazobactam IV, renal dose adjusted to 3.375 g q6h with creatinine 1.6.
3. Remove central line tomorrow if peripheral access adequate; Foley out tonight, monitor for retention given BPH.
4. Repeat blood culture drawn 16:10 to document clearance.
5. Restart heparin ppx now that platelets 112,000.
6. Hold metformin and lisinopril until creatinine at or near baseline.
7. Renal US already without obstruction; no repeat imaging unless fever recurs.
8. Family updated by phone 16:20.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD3
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Length of stay: 3 days, discharged HD3 at 15:20.

Discharge diagnoses: 1) Septic shock, resolved 2) E. coli bacteremia 3) Acute pyelonephritis 4) AKI on normal baseline, improving 5) Sepsis-associated thrombocytopenia, resolving 6) T2DM 7) HTN 8) BPH.
HOSPITAL COURSE:
56-year-old male presented at 02:10 HD1 with 4 days of dysuria followed by rigors, right flank pain, and confusion. Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
Lactate 4.2 mmol/L at 02:10, 3.6 mmol/L repeat at 05:30. Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics.
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61. Post-bolus vitals at 04:45: HR 118, BP 88/50, RR 26, T 38.9 C.
Norepinephrine started at 04:50 at 0.05 mcg/kg/min, titrated to 0.12 mcg/kg/min to keep MAP above 65. Weaned off HD2 at 12:40.
Blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours, pan-sensitive including to ceftriaxone and ciprofloxacin. Vancomycin stopped HD2.
Repeat blood cultures from HD2 16:10 show no growth to date at discharge.
Renal function improved to creatinine 1.3 mg/dL on HD3; platelets 138,000; WBC 9,800; afebrile more than 36 h.
Foley removed HD2 evening, voided spontaneously 240 mL, no retention. Central line removed HD3 09:00, tip site clean.
Ambulating independently, tolerating regular diabetic diet, pain 1/10.
DISCHARGE VITALS (14:30): T 36.9 C, HR 78, BP 122/72, RR 16, SpO2 98 percent room air.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID to complete 14 total days of therapy for bacteremic pyelonephritis.
Atorvastatin 20 mg PO nightly - resume.
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO nightly - resume.
Lisinopril 20 mg PO daily - HOLD until repeat creatinine reviewed by primary clinician.
Metformin 1000 mg PO BID - HOLD, resume when creatinine at baseline.
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO q6h PRN pain.
FOLLOW-UP:
Primary care in 5-7 days with BMP and CBC drawn beforehand.
Urology in 3-4 weeks for evaluation of BPH and prior nephrolithiasis.
RETURN PRECAUTIONS: fever above 38.0 C, recurrent flank pain, vomiting preventing oral intake, decreased urination, lightheadedness, or confusion.
Pt and wife given written instructions and verbalized understanding at 15:05. Discharged home with wife, ambulatory.
